title: Authority-bound semantic audit of real F-GC30/F-GC33 coupling coefficient u
conclusions: The production authority defines u as an inverse accepted-trajectory sensitivity, not from the accepted storage-change ledger.
In the qualified real-Richards F-GC44 predictor, total physical storage change is zero while u is nonzero.
Therefore u cannot generally be identified with physical water storage, even though it has the algebraic role and dimension of a coupling storage coefficient.
The nonzero u with zero net storage change is consistent with a through-flow response: equal total input and output can leave inventory unchanged while the lower-face head remains sensitive to q_bot.
F-GC33 is an exact affine unit/area transformation and does not add a new physical interpretation to u.
limits: This is a retrospective semantic reanalysis of one already-qualified near-equilibrium real-SWAP fixture, not a broad hydrological-envelope qualification.
It does not show that u contains no storage information; it shows only that u is not identical to net physical storage change.
No production coupling change follows from this evidence alone.
next: Prospectively scan real F-GC44 predictor responses over predeclared duration and q_bot values, comparing u, q_u, head response, total storage change and independent mass ledgers.
